title: Sistema Taj Mahal - Marcelin Nebenhaus 2017
credits: Sistema Taj Mahal, Xpu Ha, Quintana Roo, Mexico; UTM 16Q E 471134 N 2265043; total surveyed underwater passages 32,669 ft (9,957.5 m); maximum surveyed depth 78 ft (23.78 m); original explorers Nancy DeRosa, Tony DeRosa, Steve Gerrard, Wayne Nefzger, unknown divers from the French Federation; further exploration by various; survey and cartography by Marcelin Nebenhaus, January 2017 - April 2017; copyright 2017 Marcelin Nebenhaus (photo of the banner at the cenote)
placementWhy: Good (about 5-10 m around Taj Mahal): free similarity fit on the three points checked on the ground for the Gerrard 2001 map (taj-mahal.json), residuals 11, 7 and 4 m; 0.427 m/px, rotated 4.2 degrees. Points: Cenote Taj Mahal's pool on the database's Taj Mahal (Open Caves source, taken on site); Cenote Mangrove's ring-shaped outline centred on the ring-shaped pond on the satellite; City of Agre's south-west pool (where the 1783 ft line arrives) on the dark open-water pool on the satellite. The banner's printed scale bar is not used: its metre and foot bars agree (0.345 m/px) but are 19% short of the ground (Taj Mahal - City of Agre 375 m on the satellite, 294 m by the bar) - the bar was likely not scaled with the drawing when the banner was printed. Its 'N mag 2017' arrow is up; the fit's 4 degrees is mostly the photo and the magnetic north. Cross-checked: Buena Vista lands 20 m from the pale gap in the canopy taken as its check point on the Gerrard map, Sugarbowl, Sacrado, Nachich and Twin Cenotes within 10-30 m of the Gerrard map's.

The cenotes are light blue pools outlined in black: their outlines are dropped (poolOutlinesPx).
